title: Exposition of Proverbs
english: Of the Lord: The gates of the wise are the practical virtues, through which the wisdom of God enters. But impurity will be inflicted upon a man of misfortune: If virtue diminishes evil, and virtue makes evil manifest, this will happen in the age to come until evil ceases; for it has been set [to be said] that 'will be inflicted' instead of 'will be corrupted'; and impurity is corrupted either by practical [virtue] or by the punishment of severity. 'Save those being led to death and being killed without mercy, do not spare' (Psalm 85:13). Use this word for those being granted knowledge and those being negligent of the teaching, many of whom are being led by evil into death.

'Eat honey, my son, for it is a good thing, so that your throat may be sweetened' (Proverbs 24:13). He who is being benefited from the divine writings eats honey; but he who casts out the words from the things themselves, from which even the holy prophets and apostles have received, chews wax; and to eat honey is possible for everyone who wishes, but the wax is for the pure alone.

'Do not bring near the impious [thinking] you are just': Do not betray God for the sake of pleasure; for this one is thought to be just, and he will by no means abandon you. 'If your enemy falls, do not rejoice': For God turns his wrath away from the fallen one, having had mercy on him; but he is angry with the one who has been puffed up over the fall of his enemy; for everyone who rejoices is like the devil, who does not want all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. It should be noted, however, that he spoke of a man here as the enemy, for whom the Lord has enjoined us to pray in the Gospels (Matthew 5:44).

'For they will not bear children of the wicked': Evil [things] will not produce virtues and right doctrines, for these are the offspring of the soul, because they do not fear the Lord; but those being in the fear of the Lord will have offspring all day long, and their hope will not depart. 'Fear the Lord, my son, and [fear] a king' (Proverbs 14:26): In order that they may know you alone...
